case: Deutsche Bank AG v. Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, ICSID Case No. ARB/09/2

parties.claimant: Deutsche Bank AG (German, Frankfurt; branches Colombo/London/Singapore)
parties.respondent: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
parties.sovereign_owned_counterparty: Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), 100% state-owned under CPC Act No. 28 of 1961

treaty.name: Treaty between the Federal Republic of Germany and the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka concerning the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments

instrument: 12-Month Target Profit Forward on Dubai (oil hedging), Term Sheet 2008-07-08, Strike USD 112.50/bbl, Strike Volume 100,000 bbl, cap USD 10/bbl upside, Target Profit USD 2.5m, payments monthly from 2008-08-01

facts.oil_price_context: Dubai USD 137.52 on signing; peak USD 140.24 on 2008-07-15; then collapse
facts.payments: Deutsche Bank -> CPC USD 35,523.81 on 2008-09-19; CPC -> Deutsche Bank USD 1,659,636.36 on 2008-10-17 and USD 4,507,857.14 (or 4,597,857.14 per dissent) on 2008-11-14
facts.supreme_court_interim_order: 2008-11-28: suspend CPC payments, order Central Bank investigation
facts.termination: 2008-12-03 by Deutsche Bank for failure to execute ISDA Master within 90 days

award.dissent: Makhdoom Ali Khan: Hedging Agreement not an 'investment' under BIT Art 1(1)(c) ('claims to money used to create economic value' + 'associated with an investment') nor ICSID Art 25; no contribution at inception; amount claimed not money used to create value
award.majority_holdings: Hedging Agreement = asset/claim to money with economic value; territorial nexus satisfied (impact, funds, activity in Sri Lanka); FET breach via Supreme Court interim order + Central Bank measures; expropriation analysis on contractual debt

damages.awarded_recorded_by_unctad: 60.00 mln USD (UNCTAD Investment Dispute Settlement Navigator, Deutsche Bank v Sri Lanka)
damages.note: Tribunal awarded damages based on close-out amount; dissent contests qualification as investment and therefore entitlement to damages
damages.interest_claimed: from 2008-12-09 to award, then to payment
damages.costs_claimed: full indemnity costs, arbitrators/ICSID plus counsel/experts

award.annulment: Sri Lanka applied 2013-03-08; ad hoc Committee (Rigo Sureda/Danelius/Kettani) constituted 2013-04-17; provisional stay terminated 2013-06-18 after withdrawal; suspended by agreement 2014-2016; discontinued 2016-09-09 under ICSID Rule 43(1) — award survived annulment

verification.two_source_check: ICSID Case Details ARB/09/2 (BIT Germany-Sri Lanka 2000, Award 2012-10-31, decided in favour of investor) + Award PDF CL-0142 (treaty text, dates, USD 60,368,993) + UNCTAD Navigator (60.00 mln USD) — exceeds two-source requirement; cross-checked via Jus Mundi/Cambridge ICSID Reports headnotes
verification.merits_vs_jurisdiction_honesty: Do not overstate: majority jurisdiction finding contested by reasoned dissent (no investment under BIT/ICSID); majority merits = FET/expropriation breach; damages calibrated to close-out; annulment sought then discontinued (not affirmed on merits). Finance-side g4 preserved as jurisdiction-plus-award instance, merits valuation qualified by dissent.
verification.treaty_year_figure_triple: Treaty 2000-06-07, Hedging 2008-07-08, Award 2012-10-31, Claim/Award figure USD 60.37m — all three from at least two primary sources each

sources: ICSID Case Details ARB/09/2 — German Claimant, BIT Germany-Sri Lanka 2000, Hedging agreement subject, Award 2012-10-31 with Khan dissent; Annulment 2013-03-08 discontinued 2016-09-09

Award PDF via ICSID (CL-0142) and italaw1273 dissent — Treaty 7 June 2000 Articles 2/3/4/8, Hedging Agreement 8 July 2008 terms, payments, Supreme Court Order 28 Nov 2008, Termination 3 Dec 2008, Close-out USD 60,368,993 (10 Dec 2008)

UNCTAD Investment Dispute Settlement Navigator — Deutsche Bank v Sri Lanka (Germany-Sri Lanka BIT 2000) — Status/Outcome 'Decided in favour of investor', Amounts 60.00 mln USD claimed / 60.00 mln USD awarded
CIL NUS / Jus Mundi / Cambridge ICSID Reports 2021 headnotes — BIT 2000, jurisdiction territorial nexus + Salini test, FET/expropriation holdings
paper_map: Second finance-side g4 alongside Abaclat: bank derivative (not bond) uses Germany-Sri Lanka BIT to convert CPC commercial hedging debt into treaty claim; majority stretches 'investment' to cover hedging agreement, dissent marks boundary (no money used to create value, capped upside USD 2.5m vs claimed USD 60.37m). Sovereign apex converts contractual K into treaty K; domestic taxpayer bears via fiscal G/P1P0 while domestic regulatory space chilled (Central Bank/Supreme Court measures found FET breach). Label as jurisdiction-plus-award instance with dissent flagged — no merits overstating.
